module.title: Cross-Contact and Safe Handling Procedures
module.description: Cross-contact and safe handling: understanding cross-contact, cleaning and kitchen safety, handwashing and gloves, and preventing cross-contact during preparation.

lessons.title: Understanding Cross-Contact
lessons.body_md:
Cross-contact occurs when allergen proteins are transferred from one food, surface, utensil, or piece of equipment to another.

Even very small amounts of an allergen can trigger a serious allergic reaction.

Cross-contact is different from bacterial contamination.

Examples of cross-contact include:

- Using the same cutting board for multiple foods without proper cleaning
- Shared fryer oil
- Shared grill surfaces
- Reusing utensils between dishes
- Touching allergen-containing food and then touching another dish

> **Important:**
> Cooking does NOT remove allergens.
>
> A dish may appear safe while still containing allergen proteins.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-contact can happen easily in busy kitchens
- Small amounts of allergens can cause reactions
- Shared equipment increases risk
- Awareness and proper procedures reduce risk

options.text: Transfer of allergen proteins from one food or surface to another

lessons.title: Cleaning and Kitchen Safety Procedures
lessons.body_md:
Proper cleaning procedures are essential for reducing allergen risk.

Simply wiping a surface is not enough to remove allergen proteins.

Staff should:

- Clean and sanitize prep surfaces thoroughly
- Use clean utensils and tools
- Separate allergen-containing foods when possible
- Maintain organized prep areas

High-risk equipment includes:

- Shared fryers
- Shared grills
- Flat tops
- Shared prep surfaces
- Shared pasta water

> **Important:**
> Shared fryer oil can transfer allergen proteins between foods.

For example:
French fries cooked in oil previously used for breaded shrimp may no longer be safe for some guests with shellfish allergies.

## Key Concepts

- Cleaning reduces allergen risk
- Wiping alone is not enough
- Shared equipment increases risk
- Organized prep procedures improve safety

quick_check.question: Why is wiping a surface not enough?

options.text: Wiping may not remove allergen proteins

lessons.title: Handwashing, Gloves, and Safe Handling Procedures
lessons.body_md:
Gloves alone do NOT prevent allergen cross-contact.

Hands must be properly washed before changing gloves and before handling allergy-sensitive food.

Proper procedures include:

- Washing hands thoroughly with soap and water
- Changing gloves between tasks
- Washing hands after touching allergen-containing food
- Avoiding contact with multiple surfaces unnecessarily
- Using clean utensils and prep areas

> **Important:**
> Wiping gloves or continuing to use the same gloves does NOT make them safe.
>
> Gloves can spread allergens just like hands.

## Key Concepts

- Gloves are not a replacement for handwashing
- Proper handwashing reduces allergen transfer
- Gloves must be changed appropriately
- Safe handling procedures reduce risk

quick_check.question: Do gloves alone prevent allergen cross-contact?

options.text: No, gloves alone do not prevent cross-contact

lessons.title: Preventing Cross-Contact During Preparation
lessons.body_md:
Allergy-sensitive meals should be prepared carefully using structured procedures.

Staff should:

- Use clean prep surfaces
- Use clean or separate utensils
- Verify ingredients before use
- Keep allergy orders separate from other foods
- Avoid placing allergy-safe dishes near allergen-containing foods

Whenever possible:

- Use dedicated prep areas
- Use separate equipment
- Minimize unnecessary exposure to allergens

> **Important:**
> Never guess whether a dish is safe.

If there is uncertainty:

- Stop the process
- Ask a manager
- Verify ingredients and procedures

## Key Concepts

- Organized preparation reduces risk
- Separation is important
- Ingredient verification is critical
- Uncertainty should always be escalated

quick_check.question: What should staff do before preparing an allergy-sensitive meal?

options.text: Use clean prep surfaces and verify ingredients
